rationale: The preregistration freeze condition requires >=24 curated families with composition-matched experimentally-confirmed non-binders.

Exact multiset-composition matching is measurably infeasible at any reachable pool scale: the full IEDB negative universe (1,234,987 records -> 709,890 distinct sequences, 672,336 distinct compositions, mean 1.056 sequences per composition) raises the matched yield only from 0.96% to 1.63% (1/200 families pass; pilot_v3b_summary.json).

Loosening to nearest-neighbour composition matching would weaken the control below the level the C1 ranking result already showed is decisive (a composition baseline beat the judge in 3/8 families), so a Phase D positive result under relaxed matching would not survive its own baseline.

Volume is not the constraint: 30,388 distinct antigens carry negative measurements, and the top-volume antigens are dense overlapping-window scans whose negatives are position-confounded (pilot v1/v2); per-antibody families do not exist in public B-cell data (12 receptor-annotated negatives vs 4,160 positives).
what_survives: The boundary-study manuscript (publication/flex_boundary_manuscript_draft_v1.md), which now also carries the measured data-infeasibility of the binder-vs-nonbinder extension.
The frozen Phase D audit chain (this directory), including the power table any future re-opening must meet (>=24 families; results/flex_phase_d_v1/power_table.json).
reopen_condition: a new experimental negative dataset (e.g. curated DMS or Proteome-scans with per-mutant binding readouts) that changes the composition-collision mathematics; re-opening requires a fresh preregistration frozen before any new data contact.
